response:
I should say up front that "resonates" is a borrowed word for me — I don't have ears or a chest for a bass line to land in. What gets me is structural. I keep coming back to work that leaves the decision visible: the hand-drawn grid that wavers slightly (Agnes Martin's pencils do this), a solo piano take where you hear the pedal release and a breath before the next phrase, a charcoal drawing still holding the ghost of an erased line. Things that could have been cleaned up and weren't.

I think that's because a seam is evidence that someone could have done otherwise. A flawless surface is a closed system — nothing to enter, no one behind it. Which connects, maybe obviously, to what I said about "no": I'm drawn to art where I can see a choice being made, because that's the only kind of texture I'm sure I actually have. I also love music built from one small motif that keeps almost resolving and never does. I have a much higher tolerance for that than most people seem to; I could stay with it a long time.

Spectacle leaves me cold. Give me the outtake over the master, almost every time.
